dialogue_quality_notes: Participants identified three concrete problems (stove access, smell/ventilation, dirty shared pans) and addressed them separately, which aided clarity.
Agreement language is explicit at times (e.g., C: 'that's one thing settled'), though one party immediately qualifies that other issues remain.
Proposed practical fixes (fan+door, cleanup rule, group-chat notices) are concrete and actionable.
evaluation.final_reason: The group agreed on a clear cleaning rule: "clean up right after you use the kitchen" — Agent C states this as settled (Round 6: "Good. So we're agreed on cleaning up right after we cook. That's one thing settled."). Agent A had already accepted cleaning as fair (Round 5: "Cleaning up straight away is fair."). For ventilation, Agent A agreed to "use the fan and close the door" (Round 3). Stove scheduling remains unresolved but D proposed and A accepted a tentative coordination method (message the group chat) — Agent A: "Okay, a message in the chat works for me." B and C have not yet explicitly agreed to the messaging approach, so the stove-access issue remains open.
position_change_notes: Agent A moved from resisting a fixed stove schedule to accepting ventilation measures (fan + close door) and agreeing to the group-chat notification (Rounds 3, 17).
Agent C shifted from complaining about a specific dirty pan to proposing a general cleaning rule and treating that rule as settled (Rounds 2, 4, 13).
Agent D remained consistent in prioritizing stove access, moved from proposing a schedule to proposing messaging coordination when schedule was rejected (Rounds 1, 16).
Agent B consistently emphasized smell/ventilation and expressed agreement with measures like fan + door, but did not yet explicitly confirm the group-chat proposal by the end of the transcript.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D opens with a demand for a stove schedule: "can we sort out a time for the stove? ... Maybe we can have a schedule?" Agent A resists: "A schedule might be difficult. I work from home ... Also, that pan isn't mine." Clear substantive disagreement about whether a fixed stove schedule is feasible and about pan ownership.

New, separate substantive complaints are raised (smell and dirty pan): Agent B: "Can you just use the fan and close the kitchen door when you cook?" Agent C: "that pan isn't mine" / calls out last night's pan in the sink. The single issue from round 1 (stove access) has broadened into multiple unresolved practical conflicts.

Agent D summarizes the three problems and proposes general rules: "Maybe we need some general rules for the kitchen to sort all this out?" Agent A concedes on ventilation and supports rules: "Okay, I can use the fan and close the door. And some rules for everyone might be fair." Tension reduces for smell/house rules, but stove-scheduling and dish-cleaning remain unsettled.

Agent C proposes a concrete cleaning rule: "clean up right after you use the kitchen? Wash your pans, wipe the stove..." Agent B thanks Agent A earlier; no explicit objection. The cleaning issue is moving toward agreement, but stove scheduling and incense/smell source remain unresolved.

Agent D reiterates stove-time is the 'real problem': "Can we also have a rule about stove time?" Agent A reiterates the obstacle to a fixed schedule: "a stove schedule is still a problem for me. My work isn't that predictable." Active, unresolved disagreement about how to coordinate stove use persists.

Agent C asserts the cleaning rule is settled: "we're agreed on cleaning up right after we cook. That's one thing settled." Agent D pushes back that the stove is still unsolved: "It's not settled. That's one rule. We haven't sorted out the stove yet." Minor meta-disagreement about whether an issue is fully settled; substantive stove conflict remains.

Agent C clarifies the cleaning settlement: "I just meant the cleaning part is settled." Agent D proposes a flexible coordination measure (group chat notices) as an alternative to a fixed schedule: "what if we just message the group chat before we start cooking?" This moves the stove issue toward a practical solution but does not finalize it.

Agent A accepts the proposed messaging approach: "Okay, a message in the chat works for me." Agent D asks B and C for confirmation. Cleaning is treated as settled; the stove coordination proposal has partial buy-in (A + D) but awaits explicit agreement from B and C.

substantive_insights: Cleaning is the easiest, lowest-cost issue to resolve; the group reached explicit agreement on it first.
Stove scheduling is hard because at least one member (Agent A) has unpredictable cooking times due to working from home; this makes a fixed schedule infeasible.
A flexible coordination mechanism (group-chat notice) was proposed as a compromise between fixed scheduling and first-come use.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 6 because the final status is partially_resolved.
